transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um, I guess the main reason is I just can’t stay on track. Like I’ll be trying to fill out an application or do something simple, and then a car goes by outside, or my phone lights up, or I’ll have some random thought like “oh, I should look that up,” and then I’m somewhere else before I even realize I stopped.

It’s frustrating because it feels like every little thing pulls me away. I’ll start with one thing, then suddenly I’m doing something totally different and I’m like, wait, what was I even supposed to be doing?
Did you have this same trouble staying focused when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, in elementary school it was kind of a thing. Teachers were always moving my seat around because I’d talk out of turn or get distracted by whoever was near me.

And I forgot homework a lot. Like I’d do it sometimes and then just… not bring it, or lose the paper in my backpack. My backpack was always a disaster, actually—like old worksheets and crumbs and stuff. But yeah, I also remember rushing through worksheets and then getting stuff wrong because I missed little details. The teachers would write things like “slow down” on them.
Do you have this same trouble focusing in more than one setting, like at work, at home, or in conversations with other people?

Yeah, it’s not just one place. Like, if I’m at home trying to do an application or something, I’ll hear a car outside or my phone will light up and I’m gone. Or even just some random thought pops in, like I should check something, and then I’m doing that instead before I even notice.

It happens when I’m talking to people too sometimes—wait, sorry, that’s kind of the same thing—I just mean my attention gets pulled away really easily, wherever I am.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?

I don’t know… I mean, I worry about stuff sometimes, like anyone does, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there worrying all day about every little thing.

Like if I have to deal with a form or some official thing, I’ll get stressed because I know I might mess it up or forget something—actually, that reminds me, I had this one thing with paperwork where I put it somewhere “safe” and then couldn’t find it for like a week—but yeah, worry-wise, I’m not sure that’s the main thing. It’s more like… things just get away from me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed معظم اليوم?

Um… down or depressed most of the day? I’m not totally sure. I mean, I have bad days where I feel kind of frustrated or just tired of dealing with stuff, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed.

Like sometimes I’ll wake up already annoyed because I know there’s things I was supposed to handle, and then I start thinking about my room being a mess—actually I’ve been meaning to clean this one pile by my desk for weeks—but yeah, I don’t think I’m feeling sad most of the day in that way.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yeah… pretty often. Especially lately, since I can’t really play soccer like I used to. If I’m just sitting around the house, I start feeling like I’m crawling out of my skin.

I’ll tell myself I’m just gonna relax, but then I’m up pacing from one room to another, like going to the kitchen for no reason, then back to my room, then checking the hallway—sorry, that sounds random. But yeah, sitting still is hard.
Do you often blurt things out or interrupt other people before they’ve finished speaking?

Yeah… I do that a lot, honestly. Like if my mom is talking, I’ll already have the answer in my head and I just jump in before she’s finished. Same with the counselor sometimes.

It’s not even like I’m trying to be rude, it just kind of comes out. Then halfway through I realize, oh, I cut them off again. My mom gets annoyed with me for that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder with persistent symptoms since childhood across multiple settings. The patient endorses clear inattentive symptoms (easily distracted, difficulty sustaining attention, losing/forgetting papers and homework, disorganization, careless mistakes) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (restlessness, difficulty sitting still, interrupting/blurting out). Symptoms began in elementary school and continue at home, in conversations, and likely school/work contexts. Anxiety and depressive disorders were not supported as the primary explanation.
